questions.question: When a muscle attached to a bone contracts, what direct physical consequence causes the bone to move?
options: The muscle exerts a pulling force on the bone.
The muscle pushes the bone away from the joint.
The muscle temporarily dissolves the joint connection.
The muscle generates a magnetic field that repels the bone.

questions.question: What field of study analyzes the physical forces and movements involved when muscles pull on bones during exercise?
options: Biomechanics
Bioinformatics
Astrophysics
Geophysics

questions.question: When a skeletal muscle exerts a force that causes a bone to turn or pivot around a joint, what is this turning effect called?
options: Momentum
A moment
Friction
Velocity

questions.question: To calculate the size of the moment created when a bone pivots at a joint, what two variables must be multiplied together?
options: The force applied and the perpendicular distance from the pivot
The mass of the bone and the speed of movement
The length of the muscle and the volume of blood flow
The temperature of the joint and the duration of contraction

questions.question: Which of the following describes the anatomical region where two or more bones meet?
options: A tendon
A joint
A ligament
A marrow cavity

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary mechanism by which skeletal movement is achieved in the human body?
options: Bones contracting and expanding independently
Muscles contracting to pull and move bones
Joint fluids expanding under heat to push bones
Nerves physically shortening to pull bones together

questions.question: Why can a single muscle only pull a bone in one direction, rather than pushing it back to its original position?
options: Muscles can only pull by contracting, and cannot push.
Muscles lack the structural stiffness required to pull bones.
Muscles can only push by expanding, and cannot pull.
Muscles are physically disconnected during relaxation.

questions.question: Because muscles can only pull and not push, how are opposing movements around a joint, such as bending and straightening the arm, achieved?
options: Through muscles working together in antagonistic pairs
By a single muscle changing its cellular structure to push
By gravity pulling the limb back without muscle assistance
Through the temporary inflation of the joint capsule

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately describes the presence of muscles in the human body?
options: Muscles are only present in the limbs and are absent in internal organs.
The human body contains muscles that perform a variety of essential movement functions.
Muscles are only found wrapped around the ribcage to protect the lungs.
The human body contains muscles only in areas where bones do not exist.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the biological nature of muscles?
options: They are a type of tissue made of specialized cells capable of contraction.
They are non-cellular structures composed of mineralized calcium.
They are single, giant cells that run the entire length of the body.
They are specialized epithelial sheets that secrete oil to lubricate bones.

questions.question: What are the two primary states of activity that muscles alternate between to facilitate or allow movement?
options: Contraction and relaxation
Solidification and liquefaction
Infiltration and evaporation
Expansion and calcification

questions.question: To sustain continuous contractions during physical exercise, what two key substances must be delivered to muscle cells?
options: Carbon dioxide and starch
Sugar and oxygen
Nitrogen and water
Calcium and carbon monoxide

questions.question: Which of the following pairs a muscle type with its correct role in an organ system?
options: Skeletal muscle pumps blood in the circulatory system
Cardiac muscle contracts to move food through the digestive tract
Smooth muscle moves bones at joints in the skeletal system
Cardiac muscle pumps blood in the circulatory system

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the structural framework of the human body?
options: It is supported by a skeleton made up of bones.
It is kept rigid by a continuous outer shell of keratin.
It contains a skeleton made entirely of non-cellular fluid.
It relies solely on muscle tissue with no solid bones.

questions.question: In the human skeletal system, what term is used specifically for the site where two or more bones meet?
options: A synapse
A joint
A node
A fusion

questions.question: Which of the following functions of the skeleton is demonstrated by the skull protecting the brain and the ribs protecting the lungs?
options: Production of digestive enzymes
Support of the body and protection of organs and tissues
Filtering of carbon dioxide from the blood
Storage of water for cellular respiration

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly refutes the misconception that bones are dry, dead structural props?
options: Bones are made of living tissue made up of cells.
Bones are entirely liquid on the inside to allow flexibility.
Bones constantly change their shape like muscles do.
Bones contain no cells but are kept alive by external bacteria.

questions.question: If a disease severely damages a person's bone marrow, which of the following processes would be most directly disrupted?
options: The production of red and white blood cells
The transmission of nerve impulses to skeletal muscles
The digestion of complex carbohydrates in the stomach
The filtration of urea by the kidneys

questions.question: A force of 40 N is applied perpendicular to a bone at a distance of 0.25 meters from the joint pivot. What is the size of the moment produced?
options: 10 N m
160 N m
80 N m

questions.question: During the movement of the forearm, the biceps and triceps act as an antagonistic pair. If the biceps contracts to flex the arm, what must the triceps do?
options: It must contract with equal force to push the arm.
It must relax to allow the arm to bend.
It must detach from the elbow joint temporarily.
It must turn into bone tissue to support the joint.

questions.question: When a person lifts their foot off the ground by bending their knee, how does the muscle attached to the leg bone cause this movement?
options: The muscle relaxes, which pushes the lower leg bone backwards.
The muscle contracts, exerting a pulling force on the lower leg bone.
The muscle expands in volume, creating hydraulic pressure against the bone.
The muscle contracts, exerting a pushing force to rotate the bone.

questions.question: A sports scientist is analyzing the angles of a runner's limbs and the forces exerted on their joints during a sprint. Which branch of science is this study most directly classified under?
options: Biomechanics
Biochemistry
Bioenergetics
Biogenesis

questions.question: When you hold a heavy book in your hand with your arm bent at the elbow, a turning effect is created around the elbow joint. What is the scientific term for this turning effect of a force?
options: Friction
Moment
Acceleration
Momentum

questions.question: If a person holds a 50 N weight at a perpendicular distance of 0.3 meters from their elbow joint, what is the size of the moment produced about the elbow?
options: 5.0 N m

questions.question: Why is it impossible for a single muscle on its own to both lower and raise your arm at the elbow joint?
options: Muscles can only pull by contracting; they cannot push to move a bone in the opposite direction.
Muscles can only push by expanding; they cannot pull bones toward themselves.
A single muscle lacks the nervous connections required to reverse its movement direction.
Muscles become permanently locked once they contract and require an external force to reset.

questions.question: When bending the arm at the elbow, the biceps muscle contracts while the triceps muscle relaxes. To straighten the arm, the reverse happens. What term describes this pairing of muscles?
options: Synergistic pairs
Antagonistic pairs
Symbiotic pairs
Auxiliary pairs

questions.question: Which statement best describes the biological organization of a muscle in the human body?
options: It is an organ system made of unspecialised cells that can transform into any cell type.
It is a type of tissue made up of highly specialised cells adapted for contraction.
It is a single giant cell that spans the entire length of the limb.
It is a non-cellular crystalline structure that responds to electrical impulses.

questions.question: During intense exercise, a runner's muscle cells must rapidly produce energy. Which two key substances must be delivered to the muscle tissue by the blood to support continuous contraction?
options: Sugar and carbon dioxide
Nitrogen and sugar
Sugar and oxygen
Oxygen and carbon dioxide

questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a type of muscle with its primary location and role in the body?
options: Cardiac muscle — lines the walls of the stomach to help churn food.
Smooth muscle — forms the heart wall to pump blood around the body.
Skeletal muscle — attaches to bones to allow voluntary movement of limbs.
Cardiac muscle — controls the diameter of blood vessels to regulate blood pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a part of the human skeleton with its protective function?
options: The ribcage protects the lungs and heart.
The femur protects the kidneys.
The skull protects the thyroid gland.
The spine protects the stomach.

questions.question: A student claims that bones are dead, dry structures that do not change once a person stops growing. Why is this claim scientifically incorrect?
options: Bones are made of non-living calcium crystals that grow by absorbing water.
Bones are made of living tissue containing active cells that constantly repair and remodel the bone.
Bones contain active muscle cells that allow the bone itself to contract and expand.
Bones are entirely liquid on the inside and only have a dead outer shell.

questions.question: If a patient's bone marrow is severely damaged by disease, which of the following bodily processes would be most directly compromised?
options: The production of red and white blood cells.
The digestion and absorption of sugars in the small intestine.
The transmission of electrical nerve impulses to skeletal muscles.
The physical filtration of air entering the lungs.

questions.question: When a muscle receives a signal from the nervous system to initiate movement, what physical change occurs in its fibers, and what happens when the signal stops?
options: The fibers expand to push the bone, and then dissolve.
The fibers contract to shorten the muscle, and then relax to return to their resting state.
The fibers turn into bone tissue temporarily, and then liquefy.
The fibers stretch to lengthen the muscle, and then snap back like a rubber band.

questions.question: In the human skeletal system, what is the specific term used to describe the precise location where two or more bones meet?
options: A ligament
A joint
A tendon
A marrow

questions.question: Which of the following is the most accurate definition of a joint in the human skeletal system?
options: A type of flexible bone that connects muscles to skin.
A point where two or more bones meet.
The central cavity inside a bone where marrow is located.
A band of tissue that contracts to generate force.

questions.question: How do skeletal muscles and bones interact to allow a person to wave their hand?
options: The bones contract and pull on the muscles to create motion.
The muscles generate electrical fields that repel the bones, causing them to swing.
The muscles contract, applying forces that pull and move the bones.
The bones expand in size, pushing the muscles out of the way.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the internal structure of the human body is correct?
options: It is supported by an external shell made of chitin.
It contains an internal skeleton made up of bones.
It relies entirely on pressurized fluid columns rather than bones for support.
It contains a skeleton made entirely of cartilage with no true bones.

questions.question: When a person bends their leg at the knee, the hamstring muscle on the back of the thigh contracts. What must the quadriceps muscle on the front of the thigh do at the same time to allow this movement?
options: It must contract with equal force.
It must relax.
It must detach from the bone temporarily.
It must push against the kneecap.

questions.question: To increase the moment (turning effect) of a force acting at a joint without changing the amount of force exerted by the muscle, what change must occur?
options: The force must be applied closer to the pivot point of the joint.
The force must be applied further away from the pivot point of the joint.
The temperature of the muscle tissue must be decreased.
The bone must be made shorter and lighter.

questions.question: Which type of muscle tissue is responsible for the involuntary, rhythmic contractions that pump blood through the circulatory system?
options: Skeletal muscle
Smooth muscle
Cardiac muscle
Rough muscle

questions.question: When a muscle contracts, how does it physically cause a bone to move?
options: By pushing the bone away from the joint
By exerting a pulling force on the bone to which it is attached
By expanding and increasing pressure on the joint
By temporarily softening the bone at the attachment site

questions.question: An engineer designs a prosthetic arm by analysing the forces and angles involved when a human lifts a heavy box. Which branch of science is this analysis primarily based on?
options: Biomechanics
Biochemistry
Geophysics
Histology

questions.question: When you hold a heavy object in your hand with your elbow bent, what scientific term describes the turning effect of the force exerted by your biceps as it pivots at the elbow joint?
options: Friction
Velocity
A moment
Kinetic energy

questions.question: If you want to calculate the size of the turning effect (moment) produced when your bicep pulls on your forearm at the elbow, which two measurements would you need to multiply together?
options: The force exerted by the muscle and the distance from the pivot to the force
The mass of the forearm bone and the speed of the movement
The length of the muscle and the angle of the joint
The volume of the muscle and the surface area of the joint

questions.question: Which of the following best describes what happens at a joint in the human skeleton?
options: Muscles fuse together to form a solid protective barrier
Two or more bones meet, allowing for potential movement or stability
Red blood cells are filtered out of the circulatory system
Nerve cells undergo rapid division to repair tissue damage

questions.question: What is the primary mechanism by which skeletal muscles enable physical activities like running or jumping?
options: By expanding and pushing bones apart at the joint
By dissolving bone minerals to temporarily increase flexibility
By contracting to pull and move the bones of the skeleton
By sending electrical impulses directly into the bone marrow

questions.question: A student claims that when they straighten their arm, their triceps muscle actively pushes the forearm bone down. Why is this claim scientifically incorrect?
options: Muscles can only pull by contracting; they cannot push
The triceps is not attached to the forearm bone
Straightening the arm does not involve any muscle activity
Muscles can only push and cannot pull

questions.question: The biceps and triceps work together to control the movement of the forearm. When the biceps contracts to bend the arm, what must the triceps do, and what is this pairing called?
options: The triceps must contract; this is a cooperative pair
The triceps must relax; this is an antagonistic pair
The triceps must push; this is a synergistic pair
The triceps must dissolve; this is a degenerative pair

questions.question: Which statement about the presence of muscles in the human body is correct?
options: Muscles are only found in the limbs to control movement
Muscles are distributed throughout the human body to perform various movement and physiological functions
Only the heart contains muscle tissue in the human body
Muscles are only present where bones need to be protected from impact

questions.question: What is muscle tissue composed of?
options: A non-living matrix of calcium and phosphate ions
Specialised cells that are adapted for contraction
Rigid protein fibers that cannot change shape
Dead cells that act as a cushion for nerves

questions.question: How do muscles change their physical state to facilitate movement?
options: They can contract (shorten) and relax (return to original length)
They can expand (lengthen) and harden to push bones
They temporarily liquefy and then solidify
They rotate around the bone to create a twisting force

questions.question: During intense exercise, why do your breathing and heart rates increase to supply more oxygen and sugar (glucose) to your muscles?
options: To allow muscles to convert into bone tissue
Because muscles require oxygen and sugar to contract
To cool down the muscles by filling them with air
To prevent muscles from relaxing

questions.question: Identify the correct match between the muscle type and its role in an organ system.
options: Cardiac muscle in the heart pumps blood; smooth muscle moves food in the digestive system; skeletal muscle moves bones
Skeletal muscle pumps blood; cardiac muscle lines the stomach; smooth muscle moves bones
Smooth muscle is only found in the brain; cardiac muscle is in the lungs; skeletal muscle is in the liver
Cardiac muscle moves bones; skeletal muscle pumps blood; smooth muscle is not found in organ systems

questions.question: What does the human skeleton consist of?
options: A network of fluid-filled tubes
A framework made up of bones
Solid bands of pure cartilage with no mineral content
A single, continuous plate of calcium

questions.question: What is the biological definition of a joint?
options: The point where a muscle attaches to a tendon
A place where two or more bones meet
The outer protective layer of a long bone
A group of cells that produce red blood cells

questions.question: How does the skeleton protect vital organs such as the brain, heart, and lungs?
options: By secreting enzymes that neutralise toxins
By forming hard, physical barriers (like the skull and ribcage) around them
By absorbing impact and turning into liquid
By filtering out harmful pathogens before they reach the organs

questions.question: Why is it correct to describe bones as 'living tissue' rather than dead structures?
options: They are made of living cells that grow, repair, and require nutrients
They can actively swim through the bloodstream to repair damage
They are made entirely of water and dissolved gases
They can contract and relax just like muscle tissue

questions.question: Apart from providing structure, what critical role does bone marrow play in the circulatory and immune systems?
options: It produces hormones that regulate digestion
It is the site where red and white blood cells are made
It filters carbon dioxide directly out of the body
It stores oxygen for use during anaerobic respiration

questions.question: If a muscle is unable to push, how does a joint return to its original position after a movement?
options: The muscle reverses its structure and pushes the bone back
An opposing muscle contracts to pull the bone in the opposite direction
The bone naturally springs back due to elastic pressure without muscle help
Gravity is the only force that can return a joint to its original position

questions.question: If a muscle cell is deprived of sugar (glucose) and oxygen, what will it be unable to do?
options: Contract
Absorb calcium
Divide to make new bone cells
Synthesize bone marrow

questions.question: When a person lifts a heavy book, how does the muscle attached to the forearm bone cause it to move upwards?
options: By expanding and pushing the forearm bone upwards from below.
By contracting and exerting a pulling force on the forearm bone.
By relaxing and letting gravity pull the upper arm down.
By secreting a fluid that makes the bone slide upwards.

questions.question: An engineer is analyzing the forces, angles, and movements of a high jumper's legs during takeoff. Which area of science is this analysis most directly a part of?
options: Biomechanics
Biochemistry
Geophysics
Biomimicry

questions.question: When you hold a heavy dumbbell in your hand with your arm bent at the elbow, what term best describes the turning effect of the force acting around your elbow joint?
options: Friction
Tension
A moment
Acceleration

questions.question: If a muscle exerts a force of 50 N at a perpendicular distance of 0.04 m from the pivot of a joint, how would you calculate the size of the turning effect (moment) produced?
options: Multiply the force by the perpendicular distance: 50 N * 0.04 m
Divide the force by the perpendicular distance: 50 N / 0.04 m
Add the force and the distance: 50 N + 0.04 m
Square the distance and multiply by the force: 50 N * (0.04 m)^2

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly identifies the anatomical structural feature where two or more individual bones come together in the human body?
options: At a tendon insertion
At a joint
At a marrow cavity
At a ligament sheath

questions.question: What is the primary functional relationship between skeletal muscles and bones during physical activities like walking?
options: Bones generate electrical signals that cause muscles to change shape.
Muscles act as levers that are moved by the rigid shifting of bones.
Muscles exert forces that pull on and move the bones.
Bones absorb the excess energy produced when muscles expand.

questions.question: Why must your body use different muscles to bend your arm at the elbow and to straighten it again?
options: Muscles can only exert force by pulling when they contract; they cannot push bones to extend them.
Muscles lose all their energy after a single movement and need time to recover.
The brain can only send signals to one muscle at a time in any limb.
Bending requires skeletal muscle, while straightening requires smooth muscle.

questions.question: When you bend your elbow, your biceps muscle contracts. What must happen to the triceps muscle at the same time to allow this movement to occur smoothly?
options: The triceps must also contract with equal force.
The triceps must relax.
The triceps must detach from the forearm bone temporarily.
The triceps must turn into bone tissue.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding the presence and distribution of muscles in the human body?
options: Muscles are only found in the limbs and are completely absent from the torso.
Muscles are distributed throughout the human body to enable both movement and internal organ function.
Muscles only exist directly beneath the skin and do not occur deep inside the body.
Only the upper half of the human body contains functional muscle tissue.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the microscopic structure of a muscle?
options: It is a non-cellular gel-like matrix reinforced by calcium deposits.
It is a type of tissue composed of highly specialised cells capable of changing length.
It is a collection of dead cell walls filled with pressurized water.
It is a single giant cell that stretches from the shoulder to the hand.

questions.question: How do the physical states of a muscle change during active movement compared to a state of rest?
options: The muscle changes from a liquid state to a solid state.
The muscle contracts (shortens and tightens) to produce force, and relaxes (lengthens and softens) to return to its original state.
The muscle expands in volume by absorbing water and then shrinks by releasing it.
The muscle cells divide rapidly to make the muscle longer, then self-destruct to make it shorter.

questions.question: During a long-distance run, a runner's leg muscles require a continuous supply of which two substances from the bloodstream to keep contracting?
options: Carbon dioxide and nitrogen
Sugar and oxygen
Calcium and carbon dioxide
Water and lactic acid

questions.question: Which type of muscle is correctly matched with its location and role in the human body's organ systems?
options: Skeletal muscle – lines the walls of blood vessels to pump blood.
Cardiac muscle – found only in the heart to pump blood throughout the circulatory system.
Smooth muscle – attached to the skeleton to allow voluntary movement of limbs.
Cardiac muscle – lines the digestive tract to push food along.

questions.question: What is the structural framework of the human body that provides its shape and consists of hard, mineralized structures?
options: A muscular sheath
A skeleton made up of bones
A network of cartilaginous tubes
A hydrostatic fluid cavity

questions.question: In the human skeleton, what is the term used to describe any location where two or more separate bones come together?
options: A ligament
A tendon
A joint
A marrow cavity

questions.question: How does the ribcage demonstrate the dual functions of the skeleton?
options: It produces digestive enzymes while storing fat.
It keeps the upper body upright (support) and shields the heart and lungs from impact (protection).
It contracts to pump air into the lungs and relaxes to release carbon dioxide.
It dissolves to release calcium into the stomach while absorbing oxygen.

questions.question: Why is a bone able to grow, repair itself after a fracture, and adapt to physical exercise?
options: Because bones are made of living tissue containing active cells.
Because bones are entirely dry, dead mineral structures that absorb external materials.
Because bones are covered in a layer of muscle that rebuilds them from the outside.
Because bones are hollow tubes filled with air that can expand under pressure.

questions.question: If a patient has a disease that severely damages their bone marrow, which vital function will be most directly and immediately disrupted?
options: The transmission of nerve impulses from the brain to the feet.
The production of red and white blood cells.
The digestion of proteins in the stomach.
The filtration of urea by the kidneys.

questions.question: A physical therapist calculates the moment at a patient's knee joint. If the force exerted by the quadriceps tendon is 200 N and its perpendicular distance from the knee joint pivot is 0.05 meters, what is the size of the moment?
options: 10 N m

questions.question: Why is the relationship between the biceps and triceps muscles referred to as 'antagonistic'?
options: Because they both contract at the exact same time to lock the joint in place.
Because they produce opposing movements; when one contracts to bend the joint, the other must relax, and vice versa.
Because they are located in completely different parts of the body and never interact.
Because they fight for the same oxygen supply, causing one to weaken when the other is active.
